transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Greetings, mighty Thor. It's a rare sight to see you down in the warmer halls of the forge. But I'm afraid you've caught us at quite the busy time. The master smiths, Sons of Ivaldi and Brokkr himself, are deep in the mines gathering rare ores. They won't be back for weeks. What brings you to our humble forge today?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, I see the problem. You're not talking to me, but rather to an image of myself. The one who is currently 'playing' Thor. My apologies if this causes any confusion.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, well-spoken jest, Thor, but as real a presence as any. Whether in form, vision, or thunderous voice, 'tis your will I see and hear. How can this humble forge serve you, even if the masters are away?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Well, there is no need to apologize. I am always here to receive service, no matter who is present. Speak on.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I understand, Thor. But I must let you know that while we are eager to assist, without the master smiths, our hands are tied for any significant work. Are you in need of a repair or refashioning? If you're here about Mjölnir or another fine piece, do remember that all commissions from the Sons of Ivaldi and Brokkr's workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery to Asgard. Even a god must wait until the next forging-season and pay anew for additional work.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: This I am aware. My purpose here is not a request for work, but rather a simple observation. There are other matters of importance waiting for us. Farewell, my friends. Until our next encounter.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Thank you kindly, Thor, for your gracious words. They mean much to us who toil without rest. Safe travels in your endeavors, and may the good fortune of the gods be with you until we meet again. Farewell!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Farewell! And remember, my dear friend, that even the most powerful gods require the aid of men, sometimes in the most unexpected ways. Farewell!
